results.summary:
Docs only, both files this task owns. The multi-board part of README's "The board in a browser" now describes what #105 and #104 actually shipped, and `docs/manual-mode.md` no longer implies the cross-repo list is hand-written.

README (section "More than one repo", the paragraphs after the `--repos` one):
- `hkb init` puts the checkout it just set up on `~/.config/hkb/boards.json`, so "the repos you have `init`ed are the repos the page shows, and the common case needs no config at all". The exact init lines are quoted, not paraphrased: `registered this checkout in ~/.config/hkb/boards.json — hkb serve will show it` and `already listed in …` (the terminal wraps `hkb serve` in backticks; the README quote carries the wording inside a code span, so those inner backticks are dropped). It says why it prints them — that file is the one thing init writes outside your repo.
- The file is still yours: the JSON example stays, a bare path is what init writes and what you write by hand (the checkout's own `.kanban/board.json` names the board, so a rename follows it), and `{ "path": …, "board": … }` — or `"~/code/infra#release"` — pins a second board inside one repo, "the thing `init` cannot work out for you". Delete an entry to stop serving it.
- The live-reload paragraph #104 wrote is kept nearly verbatim (once per poll interval, no restart, no GitHub call, a board already there keeps its cached cards, a stale entry is a warning and a skip), plus the `--repos` sentence: overrides the list, does not reload.
- "Nothing is scanned for" became its own closing paragraph with the distinction the task asked for: hkb never crawls your filesystem, and a checkout that registers itself is not an exception — running `hkb init` in a directory *is* the act of naming it.

`docs/manual-mode.md:48-50`: "(or list them once in `~/.config/hkb/boards.json` and just run `hkb serve`)" became plain `hkb serve` already doing it, because init registers every checkout and the server re-reads the list while it runs.

The stale sentence #96/#97 added was already gone — #104's worker removed it when the behaviour changed — so `rg -n "read once, while .hkb serve. starts" README.md docs/` was already empty before this change and still is.
